lines.text: Your code wants one shape. The vendor's SDK hands you a different one.
An adapter lets them talk, and neither side changes. It converts one interface into another.
A factory picks which thing to build. An adapter reshapes a thing that already exists.
That seam is where your domain stops and the vendor starts. Nothing in your code knows their client exists.
The domain asks for amount, then currency. The vendor wants them the other way round, under a different name.
The answer gets converted too, back into a type you own. Every difference handled in one box.
It costs a layer you maintain on both sides. It pays when the two shapes change for different reasons.
It leaks when the vendor's response type shows up in your caller's signature. Then the whole seam is decoration.
Stacked adapters fail the same way, one layer down. Keep one box per pair of shapes and finish the translation inside it.
